RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT. Full text in the session log, section 2 / RT7-AC2.

1. WHAT CAN STILL RECONCILE AND BE WRONG. THREE CLASSES, none closed by the holdouts. (i) MISATTRIBUTION INSIDE A SLEEVE: COT's TARGET nodes are custody_value x recursive_model_weight, so a wrong blend weight still sums to the account's custody value and reconciles exactly. THE FIXTURE THAT WOULD CATCH IT DOES NOT EXIST AND IS BUILDABLE: perturb ONE fact_model_blend.relative_allocation on a real account and assert the per-leaf values MOVE. Nothing in this cell asserts a leaf's value against an independently-derived expectation -- expand_model is tested for cycles, missing nodes and retained mass, not for arithmetic against a second source. (ii) THE OBSERVED/TARGET CONFUSION AT THE READER: 49F's model node is ASSIGNED at full account value, COT's are TARGET; both sit under an OBSERVED account and both sum to it, so a consumer that renders children without reading `basis` shows a model target as a holding -- the endpoint's own forbidden shape -- while every total reconciles. The fixture is a FNTEND render assertion that `basis` reaches the label, which is IRPT_FNTEND's to build. (iii) A WHOLE-FIRM STALE SHIFT: if the custody feed is a day behind, every number is internally consistent and uniformly wrong. The two clocks now make the condition VISIBLE, but carrying a clock is not checking it: nothing refuses a snapshot whose custody clock is N days behind the business date, and the tolerance that would define N does not exist as a declared value anywhere in this project.

2. WHICH FIRM'S OVERLAY CLOCK IS FURTHEST FROM ITS CUSTODY CLOCK. COTTONWOOD, BY ONE DAY: custody_as_of 2026-09-10 (fact_holdings) vs overlay_as_of 2026-09-11 (fact_model_assignment), measured on the landed snapshot and carried on all 971 nodes. 49F and INF read 2026-09-11 for both -- and for 49F that is STRUCTURAL rather than reassuring: its custody and overlay arrive in ONE table (fact_allocation_account_map), so the two clocks CANNOT differ there and equality is not evidence of freshness. WHAT THE SNAPSHOT SAYS ABOUT COT'S GAP IS: the two dates, on the header and on every node, and nothing else. It does NOT say the gap is acceptable and does NOT say what it means. Concretely: COT's TARGET attribution is computed from a model assignment dated one day AFTER the holdings it attributes, so an account rebalanced on the 11th has its 10th-of-the-month custody value attributed to its NEW model, and every total still reconciles. The condition was invisible before this cell; whether it is tolerable belongs to whoever owns the COT feed cadence, and a tolerance invented by a worker would become a fact by repetition.

3. WHAT THE SERVED SLICE CANNOT TELL A READER ABOUT EXCLUDED ACCOUNTS. It reports coverage.remainder -- the excluded NODE count and their summed custody value -- and that is deliberately all. It CANNOT say: how many distinct ACCOUNTS those nodes belonged to (an account contributes between one and hundreds of nodes, so the node count is not an account count); WHY an account is excluded -- not-entitled and ownership-map-not-caught-up read identically as "not in the permitted set", which is exactly the UNPROJECTED-ID vs NOT-IN-DIRECTORY distinction _scope.unmatched_reasons makes at the SCOPE layer and the slice does not carry forward; or whether the firm holds accounts THIS SNAPSHOT NEVER BUILT -- the 134 COT and 17 49F accounts present in one producer and not the other are invisible to a reader of any slice, because they are absent from the snapshot the slice is cut from. A reader asking "am I seeing everything" gets an answer to the narrower question "of what this snapshot held, how much did your scope exclude", and the difference between the two questions is not stated in the payload.
